When you don't understand

Non capisco.I don't understand.

English needs \"don't\" to make a sentence negative. Italian needs just one little word, non, placed before the verb: non capisco. Learn this one too, as a single block: non lo so (I don't know).

Può ripetere, per favore?Can you repeat that, please?

Two more rescue phrases: Più lentamente, per favore (more slowly, please) and Parla inglese? (do you speak English?).

", "

Asking where something is

Dov'è…? means \"where is…?\". Start with scusi to get someone's attention.

Scusi, dov'è il bagno?Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

The most common answers: è qui (it's here), è lì (it's over there), a destra (on the right), a sinistra (on the left).

Easy one: il bagno is singular, just like \"the bathroom\" or \"the toilet\" in English.

why: Fourth lesson: rescue phrases. Being able to say you didn't understand and to ask someone to repeat takes away the fear of speaking, right from the start.
